name: AA Amyloidosis

criteria.description: Tissue biopsy positive for amyloid (Congo red staining with apple-green birefringence under polarized light)
Amyloid typing confirming AA protein (immunohistochemistry, mass spectrometry, or immunoelectron microscopy)
Underlying chronic inflammatory condition (RA, IBD, chronic infections, FMF, etc.)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Tissue biopsy showing Congo red positive amyloid deposits with AA protein confirmation by typing. Underlying inflammatory condition present in most but not all cases.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Most common form of systemic amyloidosis worldwide, though AL amyloidosis is more common in Western countries. Kidney is the most commonly affected organ.

pathognomonic.notes: Most common presenting manifestation; typically non-selective proteinuria

rare.symptomName: Cardiac involvement (rare in AA, unlike AL)
rare.notes: Cardiac involvement is uncommon in AA, distinguishing it from AL amyloidosis

laboratory: Elevated ESR and CRP (reflecting underlying inflammation)
Congo red stain with apple-green birefringence on biopsy
imaging: Renal ultrasound: normal or enlarged kidneys initially; small kidneys in advanced disease
SAP (serum amyloid P component) scintigraphy: demonstrates amyloid deposits in organs (available in specialized centers)
genetic: SAA1 gene polymorphisms affect risk (SAA1.1 allele associated with increased risk)
Underlying genetic conditions: MEFV gene (FMF), TNFRSF1A (TRAPS) may predispose
other: Abdominal fat pad aspiration: least invasive biopsy (sensitivity ~70-80%)
Renal biopsy: gold standard for renal amyloidosis; mesangial and vascular deposits
Mass spectrometry for definitive amyloid typing (laser microdissection/mass spec)

distinguishingFeatures: AL amyloidosis has monoclonal light chains on serum/urine
AL more commonly causes cardiac involvement and macroglossia
Amyloid typing distinguishes AA from AL protein
Diabetic nephropathy occurs in context of long-standing diabetes
Different histological pattern on renal biopsy
Membranous nephropathy has subepithelial immune deposits
Anti-PLA2R antibodies positive in primary membranous

redFlags: Nephrotic syndrome in patient with chronic inflammatory disease
GI hemorrhage from mucosal amyloid deposits
Adrenal crisis from bilateral adrenal infiltration
references: Lachmann HJ, et al. Natural history and outcome in systemic AA amyloidosis. N Engl J Med. 2007;356(23):2361-2371.
Papa R, Bhatt DL. AA amyloidosis. Lancet. 2023;402(10409):1253-1267.
Wechalekar AD, et al. Systemic amyloidosis. Lancet. 2016;387(10038):2641-2654.
